general_notes: Across states the candidates fall into recurring types: (1) the target with a thin flat border (near-identical); (2) the full target frame but blurred/low-resolution; (3) in-app vignette versions with the full character (several per state, often indistinguishable from each other at this resolution, small differences mainly in ember density); (4) tight zoomed crops that cut off legs/feet; (5) a smooth CG/vector reinterpretation that does not match the painting. For P4 I penalised vignette versions moderately for the smaller character, loss of painted background and signature, and heavily penalised crops. The grey square patch in the depleted target appears to be part of the reference image; I did not penalise candidates that omit it under character dimensions. Motion judgments come from six static frames per sequence, so timing smoothness, looping and flicker artefacts between frames cannot be fully assessed; differences between frames were small in all sequences, which limits confidence in A1/A4 scores.
